In March this year, Apple announced it would discontinue the Mac Pro and confirmed there were no plans to release future Mac Pro hardware.

A new report published by Bloomberg today sheds more light on Apple's Mac Pro strategy and reveals a surprising detail about a project Apple once had in development...

The inside story of Apple shelving the Mac Pro plans

In the latest issue of his "Power On" newsletter, Mark Gurman explains that internally at Apple, "discontinuing the Mac Pro was not always the plan." Gurman reiterates a point from previous reports: Apple's original idea was to position a chip called "Extreme" above the "Ultra" chip.

The report states: "Apple is said to have developed M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme chips, but ultimately shelved these projects due to cost and demand considerations."

Regarding specific Mac Pro hardware development, Gurman says Apple had two models (codenamed J170 and J190) in development, but they were ultimately never released to market.

Perhaps the most interesting detail in the report is that one of the two used an Intel processor:

Apple ultimately discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removed it from its official website, and directed buyers to purchase the Mac Studio instead. Although signs of this outcome had long been apparent, for supporters of Mac Pro hardware, it still marks the somber end of an era.

What do you think of Apple's decision to close the Mac Pro product line without releasing an "Extreme" chip in the Apple Silicon era? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
